layout: one column per statistic (control mean, level, p-value, % control mean, N)
naive p-values in brackets in their own column
indented index components under a bold index row
tags.picture_matters: The text layer shifts values against the row labels: it prints 'PW is Depressed' beside the life-satisfaction numbers (6.436, 0.353) and moves the -0.063 and 0.056 estimates down beside 'School Enrollment', and it detaches the % column from its rows. Pairing of label, level and % must come from the picture.

context_needed: Single arm: the TUP 'big push' package for ultra-poor women in Afghanistan, estimand ITT (PDF p. 19, equation (1)). Time point: the endline, five years after the asset transfer, shortly before August 2021 (PDF p. 5, footnote 2). PW = primary woman; school enrolment is measured on children aged 6-18 (table notes). Normalised versions of the three components are in Online Appendix Table A9, not in this table.

stored_rows.note: Index normalised to the control SD (control mean 0.000, SD 1.000); the coefficient is in SD units. No % of control mean is printed for indices. Convention (set by the reviewer, 21 Nov 2026): an outcome that is itself a z-score index is stored as effect_type 'main' with the unit in the outcome label. 'standardised effect size' is kept for a column that converts a raw effect into SD units, such as 'Effect SD of CG'.

rule: A '% Control Mean' column is a second effect for the same outcome: store it as its own row with effect_type 'percent change vs control mean' and the value in percent (5, not 0.05), never as a level, and keep its sign (-7%). Indented rows here are components of the index above them, so each is its own outcome, not a subgroup.
